## Natural history notes

A small streaky sparrow characterized by brown upperparts, pale underparts with fine dark streaking, a short notched tail, and often a yellowish spot in front of the eye. In Florida, it is mostly a winter visitor found in open grassy habitats, including prairies, pastures, marsh edges, coastal dunes, agricultural fields, roadsides, and sparse lawns. It feeds mainly on seeds during the nonbreeding season, but also takes insects and other small invertebrates, usually foraging low on the ground while staying close to grasses or other cover.
